//: Reference for every key and its default. Do NOT copy this file wholesale: `npm run setup` creates ~/.config/ccserver/sandbox.config.json for you, and copying this one verbatim would turn your config into this reference's choices rather than yours. Edit ~/.config/ccserver/sandbox.config.json (or set CCSERVER_SANDBOX_CONFIG) and restart ccserver. Use `npm run setup -- --yes --seed-example` if you do want this file as your starting point. Settings changeable from the Web UI live in the SQLite settings table instead -- see docs-site reference/configuration-model.
//backend: Linux only. The DEFAULT backend for sandboxed launches: the launch options can pick bwrap or the VM per launch (sandboxOpts.backend), and a picked backend that cannot run on this host refuses the launch rather than falling back. "bwrap" (default): namespace sandbox (bubblewrap). "qemu": each sandboxed session runs in its own KVM virtual machine (server/ws/sandbox-qemu.js) -- a separate kernel, a throwaway rootfs built from a golden Debian image, and the project dir + persistent HOME shared in via virtiofs. Requires qemu-system-x86, qemu-utils and virtiofsd, /dev/kvm access for the ccserver user (kvm group), and a golden image built once with `node server/cli/qemu-image-build.js`. Networking: the VM's NIC is attached to the per-session Go broker (ccserver-netbroker, a separate repository; fetch it with `npm run fetch:netbroker`), which runs the VM's entire network in userspace -- nothing is installed or configured in the guest, and QEMU itself has no network access (it runs confined in bwrap). The broker always starts 'open'; the running-session toggle flips it to enforce (allow-list only) and back. The qemu-only keys network.mitm / rules / dlp / inject / log configure that broker (see the ccserver-netbroker README); HTTPS interception (network.mitm.enabled) defaults to ON for qemu -- set it to false explicitly to fall back to SNI-only judging. Host services reach the VM through broker service addresses (10.0.2.100, outside network policy; only ccserver's own brokers) and appear at the same in-sandbox paths as under bwrap: gitBroker (HTTPS credentials, gh, commit signing), commitMessageGuard, sshAgent (opt-in) and the MCP bridges. A persistent (shared) VM gets each session's own gitBroker / commit signing / commitMessageGuard over that session's ssh login instead. git over SSH is not supported in the VM (HTTPS remotes only): the broker judges a raw SSH connection by destination IP, so it is refused unless that IP is allow-listed. Not available in the VM (warned, launched without): docker, tools. Agents (claude / opencode / codex): the host's own install is shared into the VM read-only (/opt/ccs-agent/<app>, self-update off) and the host's agent config dirs (~/.claude etc.) are NOT shared; no credential enters the VM -- the guest gets a placeholder and the broker injects the real one (Settings > VM > エージェントの認証; currently claude's `claude setup-token` token, which needs network.mitm on). Env var CCSERVER_SANDBOX_BACKEND overrides this.
//qemu: Per-VM resources for backend "qemu": memoryMiB (default 4096), cpus (2), diskGiB (32, the throwaway rootfs overlay -- sparse, only used blocks take space), bootTimeoutSec (120). These are the fallback: a VM template (Settings > QEMU VM) picked at launch, or the default template, overrides them.
//docker: true (default): start an isolated rootless dockerd inside the Linux bwrap sandbox. false: no docker (lighter, no rootlesskit).
//persistentHome: true (default): keep a persistent writable HOME per project (under ~/.local/share/ccserver-sandbox/home/<project>, which `npm run setup` leaves in place by design) so tools/caches installed inside the sandbox survive a session relaunch. A launch dialog offers to reuse the previous sandbox or start fresh (which wipes that HOME). false: legacy fresh-tmpfs HOME every session.
//gitBroker: true (default): git HTTPS/SSH access inside the sandbox is scoped to the repos actually related to the session (its own remotes + checked-out submodules, computed once at launch). `gh` is not disabled but rewired: gh invocations are relayed to the host broker, which executes a safelisted subset of subcommands for real (pr/issue/release/workflow/repo-view) against the same allow-list, and refuses everything else (gh api, gh auth, gh repo clone/fork/create, etc.) -- see README 'gh broker' for the exact list. No config needed for the common case -- this replaces the old approach of binding ~/.config/gh and ~/.ssh directly, which is no longer supported (those paths are never exposed, regardless of this flag or of `binds` below). Set false to turn off the broker/gate entirely (git still works, just unscoped if sshAgent is also on; gh runs unwrapped but has no credentials since ~/.config/gh stays blocked). NOT a hard boundary when docker:true (the default) AND sshAgent:true: a container started via `docker run` inside the sandbox doesn't inherit the ssh/gh wrappers and can mount the forwarded ssh-agent socket directly, bypassing the scoping. See README 'Known limitations'.
//commitMessageGuard: enabled: true (default): a `git commit` inside the sandbox whose message matches a blocked pattern is refused via a commit-msg hook (core.hooksPath, injected without touching ~/.gitconfig -- see commitGuard.js). Built-in patterns (always on, not listed here): a `Claude-Session:` trailer, and a bare `https://claude.ai/code/session_...` URL -- either would hand out live access to the conversation that produced the commit. Independent of gitBroker above (this is about local commit CONTENT, not network credential scope) -- it stays on even with gitBroker:false, and vice versa. blockedPatterns: [] (default) -- extra regex source strings (JS RegExp, compiled with flags 'im') to block in addition to the built-ins, e.g. a `Co-Authored-By: ... noreply@anthropic.com` trailer, which is deliberately NOT built in since many workflows want it kept. A pattern that fails to compile is logged and skipped, not fatal. Known limitation (same posture as gitBroker): `git commit --no-verify`, or a locally overridden `core.hooksPath`/`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, bypasses this entirely -- see README 'Known limitations'. When gitBroker is ALSO on, the same patterns are additionally checked against `gh pr create`/`edit`/`comment`/`review`'s title/body/--body-file (see ghAllowlist.js's extractGhTextFields + git-broker.js's findBlockedGhText) -- a git commit-msg hook never sees gh's own free-form PR text, so without this a `gh pr create --body "...Claude-Session: ..."` would sail straight through untouched. This gh-side check is unavailable with gitBroker:false (gh isn't broker-relayed at all then).
//ghUsageRecording: Issue #198 の任意・ローカル集計 (既定: 無効)。{ "enabled": true, "file": "/absolute/path/gh-usage-recording.json" } を指定して起動した新規サンドボックスセッションだけが、gitBroker 経由の gh 実行を固定カテゴリのカウンタとして保存する。gh の argv・owner/repo・URL・本文・パス・出力・認証情報・識別子は保存せず、ccserver が送信・アップロードすることもない。`node server/cli/gh-usage-report.js enable --file ...` / `show` / `reset` / `disable` で管理する。file は絶対パス必須。SECURITY: セッションの cwd 配下にならない場所に置くこと。browseRoots を設定している場合のみ、有効な集計ファイルが browseRoots 配下だと ccserver は起動を拒否する (enable も同条件で拒否)。browseRoots 未設定だとこの検査は働かず、既定の保存先 (sandbox.config.json 隣 = 通常は repo 内) も保護されないため、チェックアウト外の絶対パスを明示すること。~/.local/share/ccserver-sandbox 配下 (永続 HOME やレビュー用 worktree が rw bind される) は browseRoots に関わらず無条件で拒否される。集計を妨げる障害物のうち自動除去されるのは通常ファイル・symlink・FIFO・デバイスと空ディレクトリのみで、中身のあるディレクトリは決して削除せず警告して記録を止める ([gh-usage] 警告がログに出る)。集計ファイルに署名・MAC は無く、書ける者は固定カテゴリ内で件数を偽造できる。詳細は docs-site sandbox/configuration.md。
//forceSandbox: false (default): the client decides per session whether to run inside the sandbox (bwrap on supported Linux hosts). true: forbid launching the agent or a shell outside the sandbox entirely -- every session is forced sandboxed, the per-session UI toggle is overridden, and a launch is REFUSED (instead of falling back to a direct unsandboxed spawn) when the sandbox is unavailable (bwrap or its required tooling is unavailable). It also blocks the /usage background capture's direct-launch fallback. A supported bwrap environment must be available on the host for any session to start.
//sshAgent: true: forward the host's ssh-agent socket (auto-discovered, preferring one with keys loaded; override with env.SSH_AUTH_SOCK) into the sandbox as SSH_AUTH_SOCK. Only needed for SSH git remotes or running `ssh` directly inside the sandbox -- HTTPS git is already fully brokered by gitBroker without it, and commit signing is the separate commitSigning flag below. Default false: a forwarded agent is standing access to the host's real keys for the whole sandboxed process, not just git, so leave it off unless you actually need it. See README 'Known limitations' for the docker+gitBroker+sshAgent bypass.
//commitSigning: true: launches default to host-side commit signing (Settings > コミット署名 holds the key; see docs-site sandbox/commit-signing.md). The sandbox gets no key and no agent socket: its gpg.program hands each commit to the host over the git broker, and the host signs only an unsigned commit whose author and committer are the key's own identity, dated now, in a repository inside the project. user.name / user.email are set to that identity. Signing asks for approval in the approval banner -- when, is commitSigningApproval below. A missing key or gitBroker:false refuse the launch. The launch menu overrides this per launch. Default false. Replaces the retired gpg / gpgVault / gpgVaultLockPolicy keys, which are now ignored (with a warning).
//commitSigningApproval: When a launch with commitSigning asks for approval. "launch" (default): before the launch; a rejected or unanswered request refuses the launch. "sign": the launch does not ask; each commit that passes the host's checks asks before it is signed, and a rejected or unanswered request fails that commit. The banner can also approve the rest of that session's commits at once. The launch menu overrides this per launch.
//tools: Opt-in tools provisioned INTO the sandbox HOME at launch, so nothing has to be pre-installed on the host OS (see README 'Sandbox tool provisioning'). Keys: "rtk" (Rust Token Killer CLI proxy, static binary from GitHub releases) and "code-review-graph" (graph MCP + CLI via a pip venv). Each accepts true (= a pinned default version) or an object to override fields (e.g. { "version": "v0.45.0", "url": "...", "sha256": "..." } for rtk; { "version": "2.3.7" } for code-review-graph). Installation is idempotent (a version marker under the sandbox HOME skips already-provisioned tools), so a persistent HOME only pays the install cost once -- a new/wipe launch re-provisions from scratch. Requires network from inside the sandbox on first install, and python3+venv present on the host (the sandbox binds /usr). The client's launch menu offers the same per-session toggle, remembered per directory; this config is the server-wide fallback for clients that don't send a per-session choice. Default here: off.
//tools-note: SECURITY: the pinned rtk sha256 covers x64 only; on other arches the checksum is skipped (with a terminal warning) unless you pin "sha256" explicitly in the object form. Pin it when running non-x64 hosts.
//binds: Extra host paths exposed inside the sandbox, on top of the project dir + ~/.claude + ~/.claude.json. mode: 'ro' (default) or 'rw'. Missing sources are skipped. ~ expands to your home. ~/.ssh and ~/.config/gh are always blocked here (see gitBroker above), so don't list them.
//env: Extra environment variables set inside the sandbox (applied last, so they override defaults). e.g. force a specific SSH_AUTH_SOCK.
//claudeBin: How to launch claude. Default: auto — resolve 'claude' on PATH and, if it's a wrapper to the real binary (e.g. /usr/bin/claude -> /opt/claude-code/bin/claude), expose that install dir in the sandbox automatically. Set this only if claude lives somewhere the auto-detect misses, or to pin a specific build. Absolute path recommended. Env var CCSERVER_CLAUDE_BIN overrides this. opencode and codex are auto-resolved from PATH and their standard install directories.
//defaultApp: Which agent CLI a new session launches when the client doesn't request one (legacy scheduled prompts, or a browser tab that hasn't picked one yet). 'claude' (default), 'opencode' or 'codex'. The launch UI's own choice (remembered per browser) wins once made; this seeds the choice on first load and covers server-side fallback paths.
//showUsage: true (default): the client shows the top-bar Usage button (Claude Code /usage spend). false: hide it entirely. The button is also hidden automatically when claude is not installed on this server (the /usage capture could never succeed).
//opencodeGoUsage: true (default): show the OpenCode Go tab in the Usage popover (quota from https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage, authenticated with the Go API key opencode itself stores in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json). An opencode CLI install alone says nothing about a Go subscription, so this is a separate toggle: false hides the tab entirely (no key is read, no request is sent). When on, the tab is still auto-hidden while no Go key exists, and a key without a subscription shows a 'no subscription' message instead of numbers. Env var CCSERVER_OPENCODE_GO_USAGE (0/false/off/no or 1/true/on/yes) wins over this file.
//hiddenApps: [] (default): agent CLI ids ('claude', 'opencode', 'codex') to remove entirely from launch pickers and the Usage button's app tabs -- e.g. CLIs installed on this host but that you haven't actually contracted for. Unlike an app the server just can't find (still shown greyed out with a 'サーバーに未インストール' tooltip), a hidden app never appears at all; there is no partial/greyed hide mode. Unknown entries are ignored. The server refuses to start if this hides every agent CLI actually installed here (nothing would be launchable) -- leave at least one selectable. Also enforced server-side at createSession(), not just in the pickers: a hidden app is refused for every new-session path (direct WS/REST calls, scheduled-prompt auto-resume), so hiding one is a real restriction, not just a UI convenience.
//usageMcp: false (default): do not inject the ccserver-usage get_usage MCP into Claude sessions. Set true to opt in. This is independent of the Usage button above.
//browseRoots: [] (default, issue #189): unrestricted -- /api/files, /api/dirs and /ws/terminal session cwds may be anywhere on the host readable/writable by the ccserver process (this is the pre-#189 behavior). Set to a list of absolute directories to confine these to that list (and their subtrees): file download/preview/upload destinations, directory listing/creation, and every session's cwd. When set, EVERY session -- shells and agents alike -- is ALWAYS launched sandboxed, with no client opt-out: browseRoots confines what the Web UI may browse and launch into, but it cannot confine a process once started, and an agent runs shell commands, so an unsandboxed one would simply `cd` out of the roots. In other words, setting browseRoots implies forceSandbox. At startup, ccserver refuses to start if its own config/data/state directories (~/.config/ccserver, ~/.local/share/ccserver, ~/.local/state/ccserver -- the SQLite DB, this config file, saved session and schedule state files) would fall inside browseRoots -- keep all three OUTSIDE whatever you list here. '~' expands to your home.
//notify: ccserver-notify MCP (通知用, 下記 README)。配信先は Discord webhook / 購読 webhook / PWA 通知 (Web Push) の3種。Web Push の VAPID 鍵はサーバーが初回起動時に自動生成して SQLite に保存するので設定不要 (購読は設定画面 > 通知 から端末ごとに行う)。RFC 8292 の sub (push サービスへの連絡先) は既定で ccserver のリポジトリ URL、CCSERVER_VAPID_SUBJECT で上書き可。discordWebhook: https:// の Discord webhook URL (空文字で無効)。設定するとエージェントの notify ツールが Discord へ通知を送れる。CCSERVER_DISCORD_WEBHOOK 環境変数で上書き可。subscriptions: 初期購読 (bootstrap)。https:// の webhook URL の配列。購読ゼロかつ discordWebhook 未設定なら MCP は注入されない。hostname: 通知フッターのホスト名を固定したい場合のみ (未設定なら OS の hostname、CCSERVER_HOSTNAME 環境変数が最優先)。attribution: false にすると通知ペイロード末尾の "_from: host · project · session" フッターを丸ごと無効化 (既定 true)。注意: 配信先を1つも設定しないと notify MCP 自体が注入されず、エージェントは人間を呼ぶ手段を持たない。

notify.//bridge: エージェント通知ブリッジ (設定 > 通知 の GUI で編集可)。サンドボックス内の AI CLI はホストの通知デーモン (D-Bus/notify-send) に到達できないため、CLI がターミナルへ吐く通知用エスケープシーケンス (OSC 777 / OSC 9 / OSC 99) を ccserver が pty 出力から拾い、notify と同じ配信先へ転送する。enabled: 機能全体の on/off (既定 false)。false の間は捕捉も設定注入も行わず、CLI の起動コマンドラインは機能追加前と完全に同一。apps: 捕捉対象のアプリ id (既定 ["claude", "opencode"])。codex は検証環境に binary が無く未検証のため既定から外してある (選択は可能、吐けば拾える)。injectConfig: 通知を吐かせる設定をプロセススコープで注入する (既定 true)。Claude Code は preferredNotifChannel の既定 auto が TERM_PROGRAM を見て解決するため、ccserver の TERM=xterm-256color では no_method_available になり何も吐かない -- 起動引数 --settings で ghostty チャネルを指定して初めて通知が出る。ホストの ~/.claude/settings.json は書き換えない。channels: 転送先 (既定 ["discord", "webpush"])。"discord" は discordWebhook と全購読 webhook をまとめて指す。captureBell: 裸の BEL も通知として扱う (既定 false -- シェルの補完音や printf の \a と区別できない)。minIntervalMs: 同一セッションからの連投を間引く最小間隔 (既定 3000)。dedupeWindowMs: 同一内容の重複を抑止する窓 (既定 10000)。maxPerHour: 1セッションあたりの時間あたり上限 (既定 60)。level: 転送時の重要度 (既定 "info")。SECURITY: 通知の中身はサンドボックス内のエージェントが完全に制御できる untrusted input。制御文字の除去と長さ上限は捕捉時に常に適用され (設定不可)、どのセッション由来かの属性も常に付与される (エージェントが送信元を詐称できないようにするため)。minIntervalMs/dedupeWindowMs/maxPerHour は配信先を溢れさせられないための上限。

//network: ネットワーク分離 (qemu バックエンド専用。bwrap では隔離なしの open egress 固定)。qemu では VM のネットワーク全体がホスト側の Go ブローカー経由で、セッションは常に open (制限なし) で起動する。稼働中の 🌐 トグルでいつでも enforce (許可リストのみ) / open を切替でき、再起動不要 (この切替は sandbox.config.json を書き換えない。open時も直結TCP/UDPは不可でproxy経由のみ -- proxyを無視するツールはopenでも直結できない)。mode: 'enforce'(既定、許可外をブロック) または 'audit'(ブロックせず判定のみログに記録。ただし deniedHosts は audit でも貫徹する)。allowedHosts: 完全一致 または 先頭ドット(サブドメイン込み、例 '.example.com')のみ受け付ける -- scheme・ポート・ワイルドカードは不可、最大200件。deniedHosts: 同じ記法の絶対拒否リストで、allow-list・live open state・audit モードすべてに優先する(最大200件)。allowedHosts/deniedHosts の保存は稼働中の分離済みセッションへ自動反映される(mode も稼働中セッションへ即時反映される)。
